title: RSE 3/12: Rise/set/transit module + full algorithm + meridian transit
description:
### Summary
Create the `src/riseset.rs` module: the `RiseSetResult` type, the shared parabola helpers `find_maximum`/`find_zero` (into `src/math.rs`, reused by all eclipse search tasks), the FULL rise/set algorithm (`swe_rise_trans_true_hor`), and the meridian/anti-meridian transit branch (`calc_mer_trans`). Expose `Ephemeris::rise_trans_true_hor` (`&self`). The fast-path optimisation and the top-level `swe_rise_trans` dispatcher come in RSE 4.

Depends on **RSE 1** (topocentric `calc` — the sampling calls `calc_ut(... | TOPOCTR)`) and **RSE 2** (`swe_azalt`/`swe_azalt_rev`).

### Files
- `src/math.rs` — add `pub fn find_maximum(y00,y11,y2,dx) -> (f64,f64)` and `pub fn find_zero(y00,y11,y2,dx) -> Option<(f64,Option<f64>)>` (parabola fit; see §Note on return convention below).
- `src/riseset.rs` (NEW) — `RiseSetResult`, the full-algorithm core, `calc_mer_trans`, and the `impl Ephemeris` method(s) go through `context.rs`.
- `src/context.rs` — `pub fn rise_trans_true_hor(&self, tjd_ut, body, starname: Option<&str>, epheflag, rsmi: RiseSetFlags, geopos:[f64;3], atpress, attemp, horhgt) -> Result<RiseSetResult, Error>`.
- `src/lib.rs` — `pub mod riseset;`, re-export `RiseSetResult`.
- `tests/c-gen/gen_riseset.c`, `tests/golden-data/riseset.json`, `tests/golden/riseset.rs` (NEW); `mod riseset;` in main.rs. (RSE 4 adds keys to the same files.)
- `docs/codebase-map.md` — add rows.

### Implementation steps
Read `docs/c-ref-riseset.md` §1 (parabola helpers), §2 (`rsmi` flag bits), §5 (full algorithm), §6 (`calc_mer_trans`), §7 (globals/constants). `RiseSetFlags` already exists in `src/flags.rs` (RISE=1, SET=2, MTRANSIT=4, ITRANSIT=8, DISC_CENTER=256, DISC_BOTTOM=8192, NO_REFRACTION=512, twilights 1024/2048/4096, FIXED_DISC_SIZE=16384, FORCE_SLOW=32768, GEOCTR_NO_ECL_LAT=128).

1. **`find_maximum`/`find_zero`** (§1): parabola through 3 equally-spaced samples. **Return convention (§1, critical):** the returned offset `dxret = (x-1)*dx` is measured from the RIGHTMOST sample (x=1 is the middle). Callers add back the bracket half-width. `find_maximum` returns `(dxret, yret)`; `find_zero` returns the 1 or 2 roots (`None` if the parabola has no real root in range). Port the exact quadratic algebra from §1 — unit-test against hand-worked parabolas.
2. **`RiseSetResult`**: `pub struct RiseSetResult { pub time: f64 }` (single JD; C returns `tret[0]`). Circumpolar → `Err(Error::CError("object is circumpolar".into()))` matching C's `-2`.
3. **Full algorithm `swe_rise_trans_true_hor`** (§5): 
   - Setup (§5.1): resolve target horizon altitude from `rsmi` (disc radius, refraction, twilight −6/−12/−18°, `horhgt` dip). Fixed-star position computed ONCE and reused across the whole sampling pipeline (§5.2 optimisation — replicate).
   - Culmination pre-pass (§5.2): 15-point sampling, `jmax=14`, `twohrs=1.0/12.0` day, 28-hour window; body altitude via `calc_ut(... TOPOCTR EQUATORIAL)` + `swe_azalt`.
   - Insert culminations into the mesh (§5.3); 6-iteration shrinking-window refinement.
   - Zero-crossing search (§5.4): detect sign changes of (altitude − target), 20-iteration bisection (~7 ms resolution — the parent task's "86µs" figure is wrong per §5.4).
   - Return codes (§5.6): OK / circumpolar(Err) / never-sets.
4. **Meridian transit `calc_mer_trans`** (§6): 4 fixed iterations, `361°/day` rate constant, upper vs lower transit via `armc0` vs `armc0+180`. Called when `rsmi` has MTRANSIT/ITRANSIT.
5. **`impl Ephemeris`** in `context.rs`: `rise_trans_true_hor(&self, ...)` dispatches to MTRANSIT/ITRANSIT (calc_mer_trans) vs RISE/SET (full algo). Do NOT add the fast-path branch yet (RSE 4).

### C reference
`docs/c-ref-riseset.md` §1, §2, §5, §6, §7.

### Golden tests
- **C harness** `tests/c-gen/gen_riseset.c` — key `full`: for `geopos ∈ {(8.55,47.37,500), (0,0,0), (18.95,69.65,10) /*Tromsø*/}`, `body ∈ {SE_SUN, SE_MOON}`, `tjd_ut ∈ {2451545.0, 2459000.5}`, `rsmi ∈ {SE_CALC_RISE, SE_CALC_SET, SE_CALC_MTRANSIT}` (add `SE_BIT_FORCE_SLOW_METHOD` to force the full path), call `swe_rise_trans_true_hor(tjd_ut, body, NULL, SEFLG_MOSEPH, rsmi|SE_BIT_FORCE_SLOW_METHOD, geopos, 1013.25, 15, 0, tret, serr)`. Emit `{geopos,body,tjd_ut,rsmi,retval,tret0}` (record `retval` so circumpolar `-2` cases are asserted as `Err`). Build: `cc -O2 -I../swisseph -o tests/c-gen/gen_riseset tests/c-gen/gen_riseset.c -L../swisseph -lswe -lm && ./tests/c-gen/gen_riseset > tests/golden-data/riseset.json`.
- **Rust test** `tests/golden/riseset.rs`: `#[test] full` asserts `tret0` via `assert_f64_eps(.., 1e-6)` (≈0.1 s); circumpolar cases (`retval==-2`) assert `rise_trans_true_hor(...).is_err()`. Add a `find_maximum`/`find_zero` unit test in `tests/golden/math.rs` or as `#[cfg(test)]` in `math.rs`.
- `cargo test --test golden riseset -- --nocapture` passes.

### Acceptance criteria
- `cargo build` + `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean.
- `cargo test --test golden riseset -- --nocapture` passes (times 1e-6, circumpolar → Err).
- `find_maximum`/`find_zero` unit tests pass.

### Escape hatch
If rise/set times fail > 1e-4 day after two attempts, STOP and report failing (geopos,body,epoch) triples with actual vs expected. Read `swecl.c:4133–4162` (parabola) and `4387–4748` directly for evaluation-order issues. Escalate to Opus after two attempts.

decisions.decision: find_zero returns Option<(f64,f64)> (both parabola roots always paired) rather than the task-suggested Option<(f64,Option<f64>)>
decisions.rationale: C's find_zero (swecl.c:4148-4162) always computes both x1/x2 roots whenever the discriminant is non-negative -- there is no code path producing exactly one root. Mirroring that exactly is more faithful than a signature implying a single-vs-double-root distinction that doesn't exist in the source.
decisions.rejected_alternatives: Option<(f64, Option<f64>)> as literally suggested in the task description

decisions.decision: Refactored calc()/calc_ut() to thread an explicit &EphemerisConfig through the whole calc_inner/calc_body_*/calc_speed3 call chain, adding pub(crate) calc_with_config/calc_ut_with_config
decisions.rationale: rise_trans_true_hor's geopos parameter must work regardless of what topographic position (if any) the Ephemeris was constructed with -- the prior TOPOCTR pipeline only ever read self.config.topographic, with no per-call override. This was the only clean way to support C's per-call swe_set_topo semantics without mutating shared state or reopening ephemeris files per sample.
decisions.rejected_alternatives: Constructing a fresh Ephemeris per rise/set call with the right topographic config (rejected: would reopen/reparse ephemeris files, likely SwissEph/JPL mmap files, on every one of the ~20+ position samples per search)

execution_record: Task was marked done without the work being committed (all of src/riseset.rs, the math.rs parabola helpers, and the context.rs config-threading refactor sat uncommitted in the working tree). Caught during a vidhi-review dispatch to codex, which also surfaced two real C-fidelity bugs (see prior comment). Fixed both, then committed everything at 8749786 -- landing was retroactive to the done marking, not concurrent with it.

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review (verdict: needs-attention, confirmed against C source directly):

1. [medium] horhgt=-100 sentinel wrongly ran atpress through resolve_atpress before calc_dip (src/riseset.rs:60-62). C (swecl.c:4415-4416) passes the caller's raw atpress straight to calc_dip; calc_dip itself never auto-estimates pressure from height. With the documented atpress=0 sentinel + horhgt=-100, Rust produced a different dip (and shifted rise/set time) than C. Untested by gen_riseset.c (only exercises atpress=1013.25).
2. [medium] calc_mer_trans preserved NONUT/TRUEPOS via the shared IFLAG_KEEP_MASK (src/riseset.rs:393/402), but C's calc_mer_trans (swecl.c:4701) does `iflag &= SEFLG_EPHMASK` — deliberately narrower than the rise/set branch (swecl.c:4425), dropping NONUT/TRUEPOS. A transit search with those flags set would compute RA/dec differently than C. Untested (gen_riseset.c only passes SEFLG_MOSEPH).

Both fixed: (1) calc_dip now receives atpress directly, no resolve_atpress call; (2) calc_mer_trans now uses a new MER_TRANS_IFLAG_KEEP_MASK (ephemeris-source bits only) separate from IFLAG_KEEP_MASK (which stays correct for the rise/set branch).

Verified: cargo build clean, cargo clippy --all-targets clean, cargo test --test golden (91/91 passing incl. riseset::full).

Everything else reviewed clean: mesh indexing/culmination insertion, 20-iteration bisection accept condition, twilight sign handling, Pluto asteroid-alias, EphemerisConfig-threading refactor for TOPOCTR per-call override.

Follow-up gap (not fixed, both bugs were in paths gen_riseset.c doesn't cover): consider adding golden cases for horhgt=-100+atpress=0, and a transit case with NONUT/TRUEPOS, to lock these in against regression.

messages.author: agent
messages.text: Added the missing golden coverage for both codex-review bugs (9fd9d5d): "dip" section (horhgt=-100 + atpress=0, using NO_REFRACTION|DISC_CENTER) and "mtrans_flags" section (calc_mer_trans with NONUT|TRUEPOS). Verified both new tests genuinely fail against the pre-fix code by temporarily reverting each fix in turn and re-running -- not just asserted, actually confirmed. Notable finding during this: the default refracted round-trip path damps horhgt sensitivity so much near the horizon (refraction flattens apparent altitude there) that testing the dip bug through that path produced only a 6e-7 day delta, under the 1e-6 day tolerance -- had to route the dip test through NO_REFRACTION|DISC_CENTER instead to get a delta (4.5e-4 day) that actually exercises the tolerance. cargo build/clippy/test all clean (93/93 golden tests). Both commits (8749786, 9fd9d5d) now attached to this task.

edges.note: Rise/set uses swe_calc with SEFLG_TOPOCTR; JPL-backend results at historical epochs are unverified until 81 is fixed
